title: Gripper for holding workpieces, in particular preforms or containers

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.
Adjacent first and second projections with a recess between them, recess depth or length deviating by at most 25% from projection length.
A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
First and second pole shoes where the magnet in gripping position makes the first pole shoe act as north pole and second as south pole.
A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
A position sensor detecting gripping position and/or release position, or a workpiece sensor detecting the ferromagnetic workpiece.
Housing with a receptacle for receiving a workpiece sensor and/or a supply line.
A manipulator interface on the magnetic gripper for attaching to a manipulator.
Housing portion designed to suppress magnetic field escape, or a shielding device to at least partially prevent magnetic field escape.
At least one projection with length deviating by at most 25% from the thickness of the ferromagnetic workpiece.
A receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.
A bevel angle of 15° to 75° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
A bevel angle of 40° to 60° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.

claims.note: The reference describes a gripper for holding preforms or containers using pivotable gripper arms and spring tension, not a magnetic gripper for ferromagnetic workpieces.
The reference describes a gripper with pivotable arms, not a magnet displaceable between gripping and release positions.
The reference describes gripper arms, not pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to a workpiece contact surface.
The reference does not describe workpiece contact surfaces or contact surface angles in relation to a displacement direction, as it is not a magnetic gripper.
The reference describes a mechanical gripper for preforms or containers, not a magnetic gripper with specific contact surface angles.
The reference describes a mechanical gripper, not a magnetic gripper with a housing extending along a longitudinal axis.
The reference describes a mechanical gripper, not a magnetic gripper with a displacement direction aligned parallel to a longitudinal axis.
The reference describes a mechanical gripper, not a magnetic gripper with pole shoes having an active structure for directing a magnetic field portion.
This reference describes a mechanical gripper with pivotable arms, not a magnetic gripper with an active structure or a bevel.
This reference describes a mechanical gripper with pivotable arms, not a magnetic gripper with a bevel or a workpiece contact surface defining a bevel angle.
This reference describes a mechanical gripper with pivotable arms, not a magnetic gripper with a bevel angle in a specified range.
This reference describes a mechanical gripper with pivotable arms, not a magnetic gripper with an active structure having projections for directing a magnetic field.
This reference describes a gripper with two pivotable gripper arms, not a magnetic gripper with a plurality of projections.
This reference describes a gripper with two pivotable gripper arms, not a magnetic gripper with projections.
This reference describes a gripper with two pivotable gripper arms, not a magnetic gripper with an active structure having a recess between projections.
This reference describes a gripper with two pivotable gripper arms, not a magnetic gripper with specific dimensional relationships between recesses and projections.
This reference describes a mechanical gripper for preforms or containers, not a magnetic gripper with a positioning device for a ferromagnetic workpiece.
This reference describes a mechanical gripper with arms, not a magnetic gripper with pole shoes.
This reference describes a mechanical gripper, not a magnetic gripper with a magnet arranged to create north and south poles.
This reference describes a mechanical gripper where arms pivot, not a magnetic gripper with a displaceable magnet.
The reference describes a mechanical gripper and does not mention a position sensor for detecting gripping or release positions.
The reference describes a mechanical gripper for preforms or containers, not a magnetic gripper with a workpiece sensor for ferromagnetic workpieces.
The reference describes a gripper with a base but does not mention a housing with a receptacle for a workpiece sensor or supply line.
The reference describes a gripper but does not mention a manipulator interface for attaching it to a manipulator.
This reference describes a gripper with mechanical arms and springs, not a magnetic gripper with a housing designed to suppress magnetic field escape.
This reference describes a gripper with mechanical arms and springs, not a magnetic gripper with a shielding device to prevent magnetic field escape.
This reference describes a mechanical gripper, not a magnetic gripper system.
This reference describes a mechanical gripper, not a magnetic gripper according to claim 5 or a ferromagnetic workpiece.

This reference describes a gripper for preforms or containers using pivotable gripper arms and spring tension, not a magnetic gripper system with a magnet in a gripping position pressing a ferromagnetic workpiece.

This reference describes a gripper for preforms or containers using pivotable gripper arms and spring tension, not a magnetic gripper system with a magnet in a release position and a ferromagnetic workpiece not pressed by magnetic force.
This reference describes a gripper for preforms or containers, not a magnetic gripper system with projections and a ferromagnetic workpiece of a certain thickness.
This reference describes a gripper with pivotable arms, not a magnetic gripper with a receptacle in the form of a groove.

overall.why: The reference describes a mechanical gripper with pivotable arms and springs, which is fundamentally different from the magnetic gripper described in the subject invention. There are no overlapping technical features.
